βίβλος.g: a written book, roll, or volume
βίβλος.long: a written book, roll, or volume, sometimes with a sacred connotation.
βίβλος.der: properly, the inner bark of the papyrus plant, i.e. (by implication) a sheet or scroll of writing
βίβλος.as:
βίβλος, -ου, ἡ (variant form of βύβλος, the Egyptian papyrus, paper made from its fibrous coat),
[in LXX for סֶפֶר, the form βύβ- being sometimes used;]
a book, a roll, used much less freq. than βιβλίον, and with a "connotation of sacredness and veneration" (MM, Exp., x), Mt 1:1Mk 12:26, Lk 3:420:42Ac 1:207:4219:19; β. τ. ζωῆς, Phl 4:3, Re 3:520:15.†

Βόες.long: Boaz, son of Salmon and Rahab, husband of Ruth, father of Obed.

βασιλεύς.long: a king, ruler, but in some passages clearly to be translated: emperor.
βασιλεύς.der: probably from G939 (βάσις) (through the notion of a foundation of power);
βασιλεύς.as:
βασιλεύς, -έως, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for מֶלֶךְ;]
a king: Mt 1:62:1; used by courtesy of Herod the Tetrarch, Mt 14:9; of the Roman Emperor, as freq. in κοινή (Deiss., LAE, p. 367), I Pe 2:13, 17; of the Christ, in the phrase ὁ β. τ. Ἰουδαίων, Mt 2:2, al.; τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, Mk 15:32, Jo 1:5012:13; of God, Mt 5:35, I Ti 1:17, Re 15:3; β. βασιλέων, Re 17:1419:16; β. τ. βασιλευόντων, I Ti 6:15 (on the associations of the word to Jewish Hellenists, v. Cl. Rev., i, 7).†

Βαβυλών.long: (a) Babylon, the ancient city on the Euphrates, to which the people of Jerusalem, etc., were transported, (b) hence allegorically of Rome, from the point of view of the Christian people.
Βαβυλών.sd: Babylon, the capitol of Chaldæa (literally or figuratively (as a type of tyranny))
Βαβυλών.as:
Βαβυλών, -ῶνος, ἡ
(בָּבֶל, Heb. form of Assyr. Bab-ili, Gate of God),
Babylon: Mt 1:11, 12, 17, Ac 7:43(LXX); symbolically, of Rome: Re 14:816:1917:518:2, 10, 21, and prob. also I Pe 5:13.†

βούλομαι.kj: be disposed, minded, intend, list, (be, of own) will (-ing)
βούλομαι.der: middle voice of a primary verb;
βούλομαι.as:
βούλομαι,
[in LXX for חפץ, אבה, יעץ, etc. ;]
to will, wish, desire, purpose, be minded, implying more strongly than θέλω (q.v.), the deliberate exercise of volition (v. Hort on Ja 1:18): c. inf. (M, Pr., 205; Bl., §69, 4), Mk 15:15, Ac 5:28, 3312:415:3717:2018:15, 2719:3022:3023:2827:4328:18, II Co 1:15, I Ti 6:9, He 6:17, II Jo 12, III Jo 10, Ju 5; c. acc., II Co 1:17; c. acc. et inf., Phl 1:12, I Ti 2:85:14, Tit 3:8, II Pe 3:9; of the will making choice between alternatives, Mt 1:1911:27, Lk 10:22, Ac 25:20, I Co 12:11, Ja 3:44:4; εἰ βούλει (cl., a courteous phrase = θέλεις, colloq.; Bl., §21, 8; LS, s.v.), Lk 22:42; c. subjc., adding force to a question of deliberation (Bl., §64, 6), Jo 18:39; βουληθείς, of set purpose (v. Hort, in l.), Ja 1:18; impf., ἐβουλόμην (= cl. βουλοίμην ἄν; Bl., §63, 5; Lft., Phm. 13), Ac 25:22, Phm 13 (v. also Cremer, 143).†

Βηθλέεμ.sd: Bethleem (i.e. Beth-lechem), a place in Palestine
Βηθλέεμ.as:
Βηθλέεμ, ἡ, indecl.
(Heb. בֵּית לֶחֶם, house of bread),
Bethlehem, a town 6 m. S. of Jerusalem: Mt 2:1, 5, 6, 8, 16, Lk 2:4, 15, Jo 7:42.†

βασιλεύω.long: (a) I rule, reign, (b) I reign over.
βασιλεύω.as:
βασιλεύω,
(< βασιλεύς), [in LXX for מלךְ, its parts and derivatives, exc. IV Ki 15:5 (ישׁב);]
to be king, to reign, rule: I Ti 6:15; c. gen. (cl.), Mt 2:22; seq. ἐπί, c. acc. (= Heb. מלךְ על; Bl., § 36, 8), Lk 1:3319:14, 27, Ro 5:14; ἐπὶ τ. γῆς, on earth, Re 5:10; of God, Re 11:15, 1719:6; of Christ, Lk 1:33, I Co 15:25, Re 11:15; of Christians, Re 5:1020:4 (constative aor., M, Pr., 130), Re 20:622:5. Metaph., Christians, Ro 5:17, I Co 4:8; θάνατος, Ro 5:14, 17; ἁμαρτία, Ro 5:216:12. Ingressive aor. (M, Pr., 109), to begin to reign: I Co 4:8, Re 11:1719:6 (Cremer, 137).†

βαπτιστής.long: the baptizer, the Baptist, epithet used only of John, the son of Zechariah and Elizabeth, forerunner of Jesus.
βαπτιστής.sd: a baptizer, as an epithet of Christ's forerunner
βαπτιστής.as:
*† βαπτιστής, -ου, ὁ
(< βαπτίζω),
a baptizer: of John the Baptist, Mt 3:111:11, 1214:2, 816:1417:13, Mk 6:258:28, Lk 7:20, 339:19.†

βασιλεία.long: kingship, sovereignty, authority, rule, especially of God, both in the world, and in the hearts of men; hence: kingdom, in the concrete sense.
βασιλεία.sd: properly, royalty, i.e. (abstractly) rule, or (concretely) a realm (literally or figuratively)
βασιλεία.as:
βασιλεία, -ας, ἡ
(< βασιλεύω), [in LXX chiefly for מַמְלָכָה מַלְכוּת;]
1. prop. abstract, sovereignty, royal power, dominion: Lk 1:3322:29, Jo 18:36, Ac 1:6, He 1:8, I Co 15:24; λαβεῖν β., Lk 19:12, 15, Re 17:12; δοῦναι τὴν, Re 17:17; ἔχειν β., Re 17:18; ἔρχεσθαι ἐν τ. (εἰς τὴν) β., Mt 16:28, Lk 23:42; β. τ. θεοῦ, Re 12:10.
2. By meton., concrete (MM, Exp., x),
(a)a kingdom, the territory or people over whom the king rules (Es 5:3, al.): Mt 4:812:25, 2624:7, Mk 3:246:23, Lk 4:5, He 11:33, al.;
(b)the royal majesty (cf. our phrase His Majesty), the king himself (τ. σπέρμα τῆς β., IV Ki 11:1).
3. In LXX (Wi 6:5, To 13:1, al.), Targ. and NT, of the Messianic rule and kingdom, ἡ β. τ. θεοῦ, τ. οὐρανῶν (Heb. מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם, Aram. מַלְכוּתָא דִשׁמַיָּא; v. Dalman, Words, 91-147; Cremer, 132, 658), the kingdom of God (on the equivalence of the two phrases, v. Dalman, op. cit., 93, 218 f.); τ. θεοῦ, Mt 6:3312:28, al.; τ. οὐρανῶν, Mt 3:24:17, al.; τ. Χριστοῦ (מַלִכוּת דִמְשִׁיחא, Targ. Jon. on Is 53:10), Eph 5:5; τ. κυρίου, II Pe 1:11, Re 11:15; τ. Δαυείδ, Mk 11:10; absol., ἡ β., Mt 4:23, Ja 2:5, al. The kingdom is regarded as present: Mt 11:12, Lk 17:21, Ro 14:17, al.; as that which is to be consummated in the future, Mt 6:10, Mk 9:1, Jo 3:5, II Pe 1:11, al. Noteworthy phrases are: ζητεῖν τὴν β., Mt 6:33; δέχεσθαι, Mk 10:15; κλρονομεῖν, Mt 25:34; διδόναι, Lk 12:32; παραλαμβάνειν, He 12:28; αὐτῶν (τοιούτων) ἐστὶν ἡ β., Mt 5:3, 1019:14, Mk 10:14, Lk 18:16; διὰ τὴν β., Mt 19:12; ἕνεκεν τῆς β., Lk 18:29; εὐαγγελίζεσθαι, κηρύσσειν, διαγγέλλειν τὴν β., Lk 4:439:2, 60; ἤγγικεν ἡ β., Mt 3:2, Mk 1:15; κλεῖς τῆς β., Mt 16:19; κλείειν τὴν β., Mt 23:14; υἱοὶ τῆς β., Mt 8:1213:38 (cf. Cremer, 132, 658).

βοάω.sd: to halloo, i.e. shout (for help or in a tumultuous way)
βοάω.der: apparently a prolonged form of a primary verb;
βοάω.as:
βοάω, -ῶ
(< βοή), [in LXX chiefly for זעק, צעק, קרא ;]
1. absol., to cry, call out: Mt 3:3, 27:46, Mk 1:315:34, Lk 3:49:3818:38, Jo 1:23, Ac 8:717:625:24, Ga 4:27.
2. C. dat., to call on for help (Heb. זעק על, Ho 7:14, al.), Lk 18:7.†
SYN.: καλέω, to call, invite, summon; κράζω, to cry, harshly or inarticulately, as animals; κραυγάζω, intensive of κράζω. βοάω expresses emotion, whether joy, fear, etc.

βαπτίζω.long: lit: I dip, submerge, but specifically of ceremonial dipping; I baptize.
βαπτίζω.sd: to immerse, submerge; to make whelmed (i.e. fully wet); used only (in the New Testament) of ceremonial ablution, especially (technically) of the ordinance of Christian baptism
βαπτίζω.as:
βαπτίζω
(< βάπτω), [in LXX: IV Ki 5:14 (טבל), Is 21:4, Jth 12:7, Si 31 (34):30*;]
to dip, immerse, sink;
1. generally (in Polyb., iii, 72, of soldiers wading breast-deep; in i, 51, of the sinking of ships); metaph., to overwhelm (Is 21:4; cf. MM, Exp., x); c. cogn. acc., βάπτισμα β., Mk 10:38, 39, Lk 12:50. Mid.,
2.to perform ablutions, wash oneself, bathe (IV Ki 5:14, Jth 12:7, Si 31 (34):30): Mk 7:4; aor. pass, in same sense, Lk 11:38.
3 Of ablution, immersion, as a religious rite, to baptize;
(a) absol.; Mk 1:4, Jo 1:25, 26, 283:22, 23, 264:210:40, I Co 1:17; ὁ βαπτίζων (= ὁ βαπτιστής, M, Pr., 127), Mk 6:14, 24; c. acc., Jo 4:1, Ac 8:38, I Co1:14, 16; c. cogn. acc., τὸ βάπτισμα, Ac 19:4 (cf. Mk 10:38, supr.); pass., to be baptized, receive baptism: Mt 3:13, 14, 16, Mk 16:16, Lk 3:7, 12, 217:29 (τ. βάπτισμα) ib. 30, Ac 2:418:12, 13, 369:1810:4716:15, 3318:8; mid., 22:16 (M, Pr., 163);
(b) with prepositions: ἐν, of the element, Mt 3:6, 11, Mk 1:4, 5, 8, Lk 3:16, Jo 1:26, 31, 333:23, Ac 1:52:3810:4811:16, I Co 10:2; εἰς, of the element, purpose or result (Lft., Notes, 155), Mt 3:1128:19, Mk 1:9, Ac 8:1619:3, 5, Ro 6:3, I Co 1:13, 1510:212:13, Ga 3:27; c. dat., ὕδατι, Lk 3:16, Ac 1:511:16; ὑπὲρ τῶν νεκρῶν, perh. to fulfil the wish of a dead friend, I Co 15:29 (v. ICC, in l.; cf. DB, i, 238 ff.; DCG, i, 169a; ii, 605b; Cremer, 126).†

βάπτισμα.g: the rite or ceremony of baptism
βάπτισμα.long: the rite or ceremony of baptism.
βάπτισμα.as:
*† βάπτισμα, -τος, τό
(< βαπτίζω) , prop., the result of the act, τὸ βαπτίζειν, as distinct from βαπτισμός, the act itself,
immersion, baptism;
1. metaph., of affliction: Mk 10:38, 39, Lk 12:50.
2. Of the religious rite of baptism;
(a) of John's baptism: Mt 3:721:25, Mk 11:30, Lk 7:2920:4, Ac 1:2210:3718:2519:3; β. μετανοίας, Mk 1:4, Lk 3:3, Ac 13:2419:4;
(b) of Christian baptism; Ro 6:4, Eph 4:5, Col 2:12 (Tr., -μῷ, q.v.), I Pe 3:21 (cf. Cremer, 130; Tr., Syn. § xcix).†

βάλλω.g: I cast, throw, rush, put, place, drop
βάλλω.long: (a) I cast, throw, rush, (b) often, in the weaker sense: I place, put, drop.
βάλλω.sd: to throw (in various applications, more or less violent or intense)
βάλλω.kj: arise, cast (out), X dung, lay, lie, pour, put (up), send, strike, throw (down), thrust
βάλλω.as:
βάλλω,
[in LXX for נפל, שׂום, ידד, etc.;]
prop., of a weapon or missile; then generally, of things and persons, lit. and metaph., to throw, cast, put, place: c. acc., seq. εἰς, Mt 4:18, and freq. ἐπί, Mt 10:34; κάτω, Mt 4:6; ἔξω, Mt 5:13; ἀπό, Mt 5:29; ἐκ, Mk 12:44; δρέπανον, Re 14:19; μάχαιραν, Mt 10:34; κλῆρον, Mt 27:35; of fluids, to pour: Mt 9:17, Jo 13:5; pass., to be laid, to lie ill: Mt 9:2; ἐβλήθη (timeless aor., M, Pr., 134), Jo 15:6; intrans., to rush (Bl., §53, 1): Ac 27:14. Metaph., β. εἰς τ. καρδίαν, Jo 13:2 (cf. usage in π., without idea of violence; also of liquids; MM, Exp., x; v. also Cremer, 120, 657; cf. ἀμφι-, ἀνα-, ἀντι-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, ἐμ-, παρ-εμ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, μετα-, παρα-, περι-, προ-, συμ-, ὑπερ-, ὑπο-βάλλω).

βαστάζω.long: (a) I carry, bear, (b) I carry (take) away.
βαστάζω.sd: to lift, literally or figuratively (endure, declare, sustain, receive, etc.)
βαστάζω.der: perhaps remotely derived from the base of G939 (βάσις) (through the idea of removal);
βαστάζω.as:
βαστάζω,
[in LXX: Jg 16:30 (נטה), Ru 2:16, II Ki 23:5, IV Ki 18:14 and Jb 21:3 (נשׂא), Si 6:25, Da TH Bel 36*;]
1.to take up with the hands, to lift: λίθους, Jo 10:31.
2.to bear, to carry, as a burden, and metaph., to endure; Mt 3:1120:12, Mk 14:13, Lk 7:1410:7 11:27 14:27 22:10, Jo 16:1219:17, Ac 3:29:1515:121:35, Ro 11:1815:1, Ga 5:106:2, 517, Re 2:2, 317:7.
3. In late writers (MM, Exp., ii, iii, x),
(a)to take away; Mt 8:17 (Is 53:4, Heb.);
(b)to carry off, steal: Jo 12:620:15.†

βάσανος.der: perhaps remotely from the same as G939 (βάσις) (through the notion of going to the bottom);
βάσανος.as:
βάσανος, -ου, ὁ (of Oriental origin),
[in LXX chiefly for כְּלִמָּה ,אָשָׁם, and freq. in IV Mac ;]
1. prop., touchstone, a dark stone used in testing metals.
2.examination by torture.
3.torment, torture: Mt 4:24, Lk 15:23, 28.†

βλέπω.long: (primarily physical), I look, see, perceive, discern.
βλέπω.kj: behold, beware, lie, look (on, to), perceive, regard, see, sight, take heed
βλέπω.as:
βλέπω,
[in LXX chiefly for ראה, also for פּנה, etc. ;]
1. of bodily sight;
(a)to see, have sight (opp. to τυφλὸς εἶναι): Mt 12:22, Jo 9:7, Ac 9:9, Ro 11:8, Re 3:18, al.;
(b)to perceive, look (at), see: absol., Ac 1:9; c. acc., Mt 7:3, Mk 5:31, Lk 6:41, Jo 1:29, al.; ὅραμα, Ac 12:9; γυναῖκα, Mt 5:28; βιβλίον, Re 5:3, 4; τ. βλεπόμενα, II Co 4:18.
2. Metaph., of mental vision;
(a)to see, perceive, discern: absol., Mt 13:13, Lk 8:10; δι’ ἐσόπτρου, I Co 13:12; c. acc., He 2:910:25; seq. ὅτι, He 3:19, Ja 2:22;
(b)to consider, look to, take heed: absol., Mk 13:23, 33; c. acc., I Co 1:26, al.; seq. πῶς, c. indic., Lk 8:18, I Co 3:10, Eph 5:15; seq. τί, c. indic., Mk 4:24; seq. εἰς πρόσωπον, of partiality, Mt 22:16, Mk 12:14. Colloq. (for ex. from π., V. Deiss., LAE, 122; M, Pr., 107; MM, Exp., x; Milligan, NTD, 50), β. ἑαυτόν: Mk 13:9; seq. ἵνα μή, II Jo 8; β. ἀπό, Mk 8:1512:38; seq. μή (cl. ὁρᾶν), c. fut. indic., Col 2:8, He 3:12; id. c. aor. subj., Mt 24:4, Mk 13:5.
3. Of situation and direction (Lat. specto), to look, face (towards), places, etc. (seq. πρός, Xen, Hell., vii, 1, 17; Ez 40:23, 24): seq. κατά, c. acc., Ac 27:12 (cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἐμ-, ἐπι-, περ-, προ-βλέπω), v. DCG, i, 446; ii, 596.

βρέχω.as:
βρέχω,
[in LXX chiefly for מטר;]
1.to wet: Lk 7:38, 44.
2. In late Gk. writers and vernac. = ὕειν, to send rain, to rain (Kennedy, Sources, 39, 155): Mt 5:45; trop., β. πῦρ κ. θεῖον, Lk 17:29; impers., βρέχει, it rains: Ja 5:17; with ὐετός as subj., Re 11:6.†

βατταλογέω.long: I chatter, am long-winded, utter empty words, stammer, repeat.
βατταλογέω.sd: to stutter, i.e. (by implication) to prate tediously
βατταλογέω.as:
*† βατταλογέω, -ῶ (Rec. βαττολ-, D, βλαττ- = βατταρίζω, prob. onomatop.; v. MM, s.v.; DCG, ii, 499b, 790a);
to stammer, repeat idly: Mt 6:7 (Cremer, 765).†

βρῶσις.long: (a) abstr: eating, (b) food, a meal, (c) rust.
βρῶσις.sd: (abstractly) eating (literally or figuratively); by extension (concretely) food (literally or figuratively)
βρῶσις.as:
βρῶσις, -εως, ἡ (cf. βιβρώσκω),
[in LXX chiefly for parts and derivatives of אכל ;]
1.eating: β. καὶ πόσις, Ro 14:17, Col 2:16 (v. Lft., ICC, in l.); c. gen. obj., I Co 8:4; metaph., corrosion, rust: Mt 6:19, 20.
2. As also in cl. (Hom., al.) = βρῶμα, food: Jo 6:27a, II Co 9:10, Col 2:16 (EV, but v. supr.). He 12:16; metaph., of spiritual nourishment, Jo 4:326:27b, 55.†

βροχή.as:
βροχή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< βρέχω), [in LXX: Ps 67 (68):9, 104 (105):32 (גֶּשֶׁם)* ;]
1. = βροχετός, a wetting (in π., of irrigation in Egypt; Deiss., LAE, 77).
2. As in MGr. (Kennedy, Sources, 153), = ὑετός, rain: Mt 7:25, 27.†

βασανίζω.long: I examine, as by torture; I torment; I buffet, as of waves.
βασανίζω.as:
βασανίζω
(< βάσανος), [in LXX: I Ki 5:3, Si 4:17, and freq. in Wi, II, IV Mac;]
1. prop., to rub on the touchstone, put to the test.
2.to examine by torture, hence, generally, to torture, torment, distress: Mt 8:6, 2914:24, Mk 5:76:48, Lk 8:28, II Pe 2:8, Re 9:511:1012:214:1020:10.†

βρυγμός.as:
βρυγμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< βρύχω), [in LXX: Pr 19:12 (נַהַם), Si 51:3 * ;]
a biting, a gnashing of teeth: Mt 8:1213:42, 5022:1324:5125:30, Lk 13:28.†

βόσκω.sd: to pasture; by extension to, fodder; reflexively, to graze
βόσκω.der: a prolonged form of a primary verb (compare G977 (βιβρώσκω), G1016 (βοῦς));
βόσκω.as:
βόσκω,
[in LXX for רעה;]
prop., of a herdsman, to feed: Mt 8:33, Mk 5:14, Lk 8:3415:15; metaph., of Christian pastoral care, Jo 21:15, 17. Pass., of cattle, to feed, graze: Mt 8:30, Mk 5:11, Lk 8:32.†
SYN.: ποιμαίνειν, to tend, shepherd, a wider term, including oversight as well as feeding (v. Tr., Syn., §xxv).

βλασφημέω.long: I speak evil against, blaspheme, use abusive or scurrilous language about (God or men).
βλασφημέω.sd: to vilify; specially, to speak impiously
βλασφημέω.kj: (speak) blaspheme(-er, -mously, -my), defame, rail on, revile, speak evil
βλασφημέω.as:
βλασφημέω, -ῶ
(< βλάσφημος), [in LXX: IV Ki 19:4 (יכח hi.) ib. 6, 22 (גּדף pi.), Is 52:5 (נאץ hith.), Da LXX 3:29 (96) (אמר שׁלח), To 1:18, Da TH Bel 9, II Mac 2 * ;]
1.to speak lightly or profanely of sacred things (in cl., opp. of εὐφημέω), esp. to speak impiously of God, to blaspheme, speak blasphemously: absol., Mt 9:326:65, Mk 2:7, Jo 10:36, Ac 26:11, I Ti 1:20, II Pe 2:12; τ. θεόν, Ac 19:37, Re 16:11, 21; τὸ ὄνομα τ. θεοῦ, Re 13:616:9; δόξας, Ju 3, II Pe 2:10; εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, Mk 3:29, Lk 12:10.
2.to revile, rail at, slander: absol., Lk 22:65, Ac 13:4518:6, I Pe 4:4; c. acc., Mt 27:39, Mk 3:2815:29, Lk 23:39, Tit 3:2, Ja 2:7, Ju 10. Pass.: Ro 2:243:8 14:16, I Co 10:30, I Ti 6:1, Tit 2:5, II Pe 2:2 (Cremer, 570).†

Βαρθολομαῖος.long: Bartholomew, surname of Nathanael, one of the twelve apostles of Jesus.
Βαρθολομαῖος.sd: son of Tolmai; Bar-tholomæus, a Christian apostle
Βαρθολομαῖος.as:
Βαρθολομαῖος, -ου, ὁ
(Aram. בַּר־תָּלְמַי, son of Tolmai),
Bartholomew, the Apostle (v.s. Ναθαναήλ): Mt 10:3, Mk 3:18, Lk 6:14, Ac 1:13.†

Βεελζεβούλ.long: Beelzebul, a name of Satan, the chief of evil spirits.
Βεελζεβούλ.sd: dung-god; Beelzebul, a name of Satan
Βεελζεβούλ.der: of Chaldee origin (by parody on H01176);
Βεελζεβούλ.as:
Βεελζεβούλ (WH, App., 159, Rec., βεελζεβούλ), ὁ, indecl.
(Heb. בַּעַל, lord, and the Talmudic זִבּוּל, from זֶבֶל, dung (Dalman, Gr., 137n), or perh. זְבֻל, habitation, but, v. DB, iv, 409 f.; DCG, i, 181). The AV, RV, Beelzebub, comes through Vg. from IV Ki 1:2, בַּעַל זִבוּב, lord of flies(LXX, βάαλ μυῖα, Sm., βεελζεβούβ),
Beelzebul, Beelzebub, a name of Satan: Mt 10:2512:24, 27, Mk 3:22, Lk 11:15, 18, 19.†

βιάζω.g: I use force, violence, suffer violence
βιάζω.long: (a) mid: I use force, force my way, come forward violently, (b) pass: I am forcibly treated, suffer violence.
βιάζω.sd: to force, i.e. (reflexively) to crowd oneself (into), or (passively) to be seized
βιάζω.as:
βιάζω (< βία), and depon. -ομαι,
[in LXX for פּרץ, פּצר, etc.;]
to force, constrain, rare in act. (poet, and late prose), but found in cl. in pass., and so perh. βιάζεται, suffereth violence, Mt 11:12, EV (but v. infr.), whether
(a) in good sense, of disciples (Thayer, al.), or
(b) in bad sense, of the enemies of the kingdom (Meyer, in l.; Dalman, Words, 139 ff.; Cremer, 141 ff.). Mid., advanceth violently, Mt 11:12 (Deiss., BS., 258; Banks, v. ref. in DCG, ii, 803 f.); seq. εἰς, to press violently, or force one's way into, Lk 16:16 (v. ICC, in l., and in Mt 11:12; cf. παραβιάζομαι and v. MM, s.v.).†

βιαστής.long: a forceful, violent man; one who is eager in pursuit.
βιαστής.as:
*† βιαστής, -οῦ, ὁ (< βιάζω), late form of βιατάς;
1.strong, forceful.
2.violent (Philo): Mt 11:12 (v.s. βιάζω).†

Βηθσαϊδά.long: Bethsaida, (a) a city of Galilee, (b) a city east of the Jordan.
Βηθσαϊδά.sd: fishing-house; Bethsaida, a place in Palestine
Βηθσαϊδά.der: of Chaldee origin (compare H01004 and H06719);
Βηθσαϊδά.as:
Βηθσαιδά (Rec. -σαϊδά), and -δάν (Mt 11:21, Mk 6:458:22), ἡ, indecl.
(Syr., house of fish),
Bethsaida, a town on NE. shore of the Sea of Galilee: Lk 9:10. It is generally supposed that a second Β. on the W. shore is referred to in Mt 11:21, Mk 6:458:22, Lk 10:13, Jo 1:4512:21 (DB, i, 282 f.; but v. Swete on Mk 6:45).
2. v.l. for Βηθζαθά, Βηθεσδά, Jo 5:2.†

βεβηλόω.as:
† βεβηλόω, -ῶ
(< βέβηλος), [in LXX chiefly for חלל;]
to profane: τ. σάββατον, Mt 12:5; τ. ἱερόν, Ac 24:6 (Cremer, 141).†
SYN.: κοινόω, q.v.

βόθυνος.sd: a hole (in the ground); specially, a cistern
βόθυνος.as:
βόθυνος, -ου, ὁ (= βόθρος, more freq. in cl.),
[in LXX chiefly for פַּחַת ;]
a pit: Mt 12:1115:14, Lk 6:39 (cf. DB, iii, 885; DCG, ii, 367).†

βλασφημία.as:
βλασφημία, -ας, ἡ
(< βλάσφημος), [in LXX: Ez 35:12 (נֶאָצָה), Da TH 3:29 (96) (שׁלה), To 1:18, I Mac 2:6, II Mac 8:410:3515:24 * ;]
(a)railing slander: Mt 12:3115:19, Mk 3:287:22, Eph 4:31, Col 3:8, I Ti 6:4, Ju 9, Re 2:9;
(b) spec., impious speech against God, blasphemy: Mt 26:65, Mk 14:64, Lk 5:21, Jo 10:33, Re 13:5; ὄνομα βλασφημίας, Re 13:117:3; c. gen. obj. Mt 12:31; πρὸς τ. θεόν, Re 13:6 (Cremer, 570; DB, i, 305; DCG ii, 423).†

βασίλισσα.as:
βασίλισσα, -ης, ἡ
(in Attic, βασιλεία, βασιλίς), [in LXX chiefly for מַלְכָּה;]
a queen: Mt 12:42, Lk 11:31, Ac 8:27, Re 18:7.†

βάθος.long: depth; deep water; met: fullness, immensity; an extreme degree; profundities, deep-laid plans.
βάθος.as:
βάθος, -εος (-ους), τό,
[in LXX for מְצוּלָה ,תַּחְתִּי, etc.;]
depth: Mt 13:5, Mk 4:5, Ro 8:39, Eph 3:18; τὸ β., the deep sea: Lk 5:4; metaph., β. πλούτου . . . Θεοῦ, Ro 11:33; τὰ β. τ. Θεοῦ (the Divine counsels), I Co 2:10; ἡ κατὰ βάθους πτωχεία, deep poverty, II Co 8:2.†

βαρέως.as:
βαρέως, adv.
(< βαρύς), [in LXX: β. φέρειν, Ge 31:35 (בעיני חרה); β. ἀκούειν, Is 6:10 (כּבד hi.)*;]
heavily, with difficulty: Mt 13:15, Ac 28:27 (LXX).†

βλαστάνω.g: I sprout, cause to sprout, make to grow up
βλαστάνω.long: intrans: I sprout; trans: I cause to sprout, make to grow up.
βλαστάνω.sd: to germinate; by implication, to yield fruit
βλαστάνω.as:
βλαστάνω,
[in LXX for צמח, etc.;]
1.to sprout: Mt 13:26, Mk 4:27, He 9:4.
2. In late Gk., causal, to make to grow, produce: c. acc., Ja 5:18.†

βρῶμα.sd: food (literally or figuratively), especially (ceremonially) articles allowed or forbidden by the Jewish law
βρῶμα.as:
βρῶμα, -τος, τό (cf. βιβρώσκω),
[in LXX chiefly for אֹכֶל ;]
food: Ro 14:15, 20I Co 8:8, 1310:3; pl., Mt 14:15, Mk 7:19, Lk 3:119:13, I Co 6:13, I Ti 4:3, He 9:1013:9; trop., of spiritual food, Jo 4:34, I Co 3:2 (cf. βρῶσις).†

βοηθέω.g: I come to the rescue of
βοηθέω.long: I come to the rescue of, come to help, help.
βοηθέω.as:
βοηθέω, -ῶ
(< βοή + θέω, to run), [in LXX chiefly for עזר ;]
to come to aid, to help, succour: absol., Ac 21:28; c dat., Mt 15:25, Mk 9:22, 24Ac 16:9, II Co 6:2(LXX), He 2:18, Re 12:16.†

βασανιστής.g: one who tortures, a tormentor, jailor
βασανιστής.long: one who tortures, a tormentor, jailor.
βασανιστής.as:
* βασανιστής, -οῦ, ὁ
(< βασανίζω),
prop., a torturer; used of a gaoler, Mt 18:34.†

βιβλίον.as:
βιβλίον, -ου, τό
(dim. of βίβλος, q.v.), [in LXX also in the alternat. form βυβ-, chiefly for סֶפֶר and the most freq. of the cognate forms;]
1.a paper, letter, written document: β. ἀποστασίου, bill of divorce, Mt 19:7, Mk 10:4.
2.a book, a roll: Lk 4:17, 20Jo 20:3021:25, Ga 3:10, II Ti 4:13, He 9:1910:7, Re 1:115:1-96:1410:820:1222:7-19; β. τ. ζωῆς, Re 13:817:820:1221:27.†

βάρος.long: a weight, burden, lit. or met.
βάρος.sd: compare G899 (βάθος)); weight; in the New Testament only, figuratively, a load, abundance, authority
βάρος.der: probably from the same as G939 (βάσις) (through the notion of going down;
βάρος.as:
βάρος, -εος, τό,
[in LXX: Jg 18:21 (כּבד), Jth 7:4, Si 13:2, II Mac 9:10, III Mac 5:47*;]
weight;
(a)a weight, burden, lit. and metaph.: Mt 20:12, Ac 15:28, II Co 4:17, Re 2:24; ἀλλήλων τὰ β., one another's faults, Ga 6:2; ἐν β., burdensome: I Th 2:6, R, txt., but v. infr.;
(b) in late Gk. (Soph., Lex., s.v.), dignity, authority: ἐν βάρει, I Th 2:6 (R, mg.; v. Milligan, ICG, in l.).†
SYN.: ὄγκος, an encumbrance; φορτίον, a burden, that which is borne.

Βηθφαγή.long: Bethphage, a village in the neighborhood of Jerusalem, on the Mt. of Olives.
Βηθφαγή.sd: fig-house; Beth-phage, a place in Palestine
Βηθφαγή.der: of Chaldee origin (compare H01004 and H06291);
Βηθφαγή.as:
Βηθφαγή (L, -γῆ), ἡ, indecl.
(Aram. בֵּית־פַּגֵּי, house of unripe figs; Dalman, Gr., 191),
Bethphage: Mt 21:1, Mk 11:1, Lk 19:29.†

Βηθανία.long: (a) Bethany, the home of Lazarus, Martha, and Mary, near Jerusalem, (b) Bethany, beyond Jordan.
Βηθανία.sd: date-house; Beth-any, a place in Palestine
Βηθανία.as:
Βηθανία, -ας (also -ιά, indecl., Lk 19:29 and in B*, Mk 11:1), ἡ,
(Heb. בֵּית עֲנִיָּה, house of affliction, acc. to Jerome, or perh., house of dates, cf. Bethphage),
Bethany;
1. a village fifteen furlongs from Jerusalem, the modern El Azerîyeh: Mt 21:1726:6, Mk 8:22 (WH, mg.) 11:1, 11, 1214:3, Lk 19:2924:50, Jo 11:1, 1812:1.
2. A place on E. bank of Jordan: Jo 1:28 (R, mg., Βηθαβαρά, q.v.).†

βαρύς.long: heavy, weighty, burdensome, lit. and met; violent, oppressive.
βαρύς.as:
βαρύς, -εῖα, ύ,
[in LXX chiefly for כָּבֵד;]
heavy: Mt 23:4. Metaph., burdensome: ἐντολή, I Jo 5:3; severe (perh. impressive): ἐπιστολή, II Co 10:10; weighty: τὰ βαρύτερα τ. νόμου, Mt 23:23; αἰτιώματα, Ac 25:7; violent, cruel (EV, grievous): λύκος, Ac 20:29.†

Βαραχίας.long: Barachiah; his identity is uncertain, perhaps father of the Zechariah killed by the Zealots in the last Jewish War.
Βαραχίας.as:
Βαραχίας, -ου, ὁ
(Heb. בֶּרֶכְיָה),
Barachiah: Mt 23:35, v.s. Ζαχαρίας.†

βδέλυγμα.g: an abominable thing, an accursed thing
βδέλυγμα.long: an abominable thing, an accursed thing.
βδέλυγμα.as:
† βδέλυγμα, -τος, τό
(< βδελύσσω), [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁקֶץ ,תּוֹעֵבָה;]
an abomination, a detestable thing: Lk 16:15, Re 17:4, 521:27; τὸβ. τ. ἐρημώσεως (Da LXX 12:11, cf . I Mac 1:54; DB, i, 12 f.; DCG, i, 6 f.), Mk 13:14, Mt 24:15 (Cremer, 138).†

βαρύτιμος.as:
* βαρύτιμος, -ον
(< βαρύς, τιμή),
of great value, very costly: Mt 26:7 (T, πολυτίμου).†

βαρέω.long: I weight, load, burden, lit. and met.
βαρέω.as:
βαρέω, -ῶ (later form of βαρύνω, q.v.),
[in LXX: Ex 7:14 (כָּבֵד), II Mac 13:9*;]
to depress, weigh down. In NT, in pass. only: Mt 26:43, Lk 9:3221:34, II Co 1:85:4, I Ti 5:16.†

Βαραββᾶς.sd: son of Abba; Bar-abbas, an Israelite
Βαραββᾶς.as:
Βαραββᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ
(Aram. בַּר־אַבָּא, lit., son of a father, i.e. acc. to Jerome, filius magistri),
Barabbas: Mt 27:16, 17, 20, 21, 26, Mk 15:7, 11, 15, Lk 23:18, Jo 18:40. (In Mt 27:16, some MSS. read Ἰησοῦν Β.; v. WH, App., 19 f.).†

βῆμα.g: the space covered by a step of the foot, a tribunal
βῆμα.long: an elevated place ascended by steps, a throne, tribunal.
βῆμα.sd: a step, i.e. foot-breath; by implication, a rostrum, i.e. a tribunal
βῆμα.as:
βῆμα, -τος, τό
(< βαίνω), [in LXX: De 2:5 (מִדְרָךְ), Ne 8:4 (מִגְדָּל), I Es 9:42, Si 19:3045:9, II Mac 13:26*;]
1.a step, stride, pace: Ac 7:5.
2.a raised place, a platform reached by steps, originally that in the Pnyx at Athens from which orations were made; freq. of the tribune or tribunal of a Roman magistrate or ruler: Mt 27:19, Jo 19:13, Ac 12:21, 18:12, 16, 1725:6, 10, 17; β. τοῦ θεοῦ, Ro 14:10; τ. Χριστοῦ, II Co 5:10.†

Βοανηργές.sd: sons of commotion; Boanerges, an epithet of two of the apostles
Βοανηργές.as:
Βοανηργές, indecl. (on the derivation, v. Dalman, Gr., 144; Words, 42; Swete, Mk., l.c.; DCG, i, 216),
Boanerges: Mk 3:17.†

βροντή.as:
βροντή, -ῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX for רַעַם ;]
thunder: Mk 3:17, Jo 12:29, Re 4:56:18:510:3, 411:1914:216:1819:6.†

Βηθσαϊδάν.long: Bethsaida, (a) a city of Galilee, (b) a city east of the Jordan.
Βηθσαϊδάν.sd: fishing-house; Bethsaida, a place in Palestine
Βηθσαϊδάν.der: of Chaldee origin (compare H01004 and H06719);
Βηθσαϊδάν.as:
Βηθσαιδά (Rec. -σαϊδά), and -δάν (Mt 11:21, Mk 6:458:22), ἡ, indecl.
(Syr., house of fish),
Bethsaida, a town on NE. shore of the Sea of Galilee: Lk 9:10. It is generally supposed that a second Β. on the W. shore is referred to in Mt 11:21, Mk 6:458:22, Lk 10:13, Jo 1:4512:21 (DB, i, 282 f.; but v. Swete on Mk 6:45).
2. v.l. for Βηθζαθά, Βηθεσδά, Jo 5:2.†

βαπτισμός.as:
*† βαπτισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< βαπτίζω) , prop., the act of which βάπτισμα is the result;
1.a dipping, washing, lustration: Mk 7:4; of Jewish ceremonial, He 9:10; in He 6:2, βαπτισμῶν διδαχήν (-ῆς), "the pl. and the peculiar form seem to be used to include Christian baptism with other lustral rites" (Westc, in l.).
2.baptism: FlJ, Ant., 18, 5, 2 (of John's baptism), and some Fathers (v. Soph., s.v.). Not so in NT, unless ἐν τ. βαπτισμῷ, in the act of baptism, Col 2:12, be read with Tr. (Rec., WH, R, -ματι).†

Βαρτιμαῖος.sd: son of Timæus (or the unclean); Bar-timæus, an Israelite
Βαρτιμαῖος.as:
Βαρτίμαιος, -ου, ὁ
(-μαῖος, T; perh. Aram. בַּר־טִמְאַי, v. DB, iv, p. 762),
Bartimæus: Mk 10:46.†

βάτος.as:
βάτος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ,
[in LXX (always masc, as in Attic): Ex 3:2-4, De 33:16 (סְנֶה), Jb 31:40 (בָּאְשָׁה)*;]
a bramble-bush: Lk 6:44, Ac 7:30, 35; ἐπὶ τοῦ (τῆς) β., in the place concerning the bush: Mk 12:26, Lk 20:37.†

βίος.sd: life, i.e. (literally) the present state of existence; by implication, the means of livelihood
βίος.as:
βίος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for יָמִים;]
1.period or course of life, life: Lk 8:14, I Ti 2:2, II Ti 2:4, I Jo 2:16.
2.living, livelihood, means (in Pr 31:14 for לֶחֶם; v. DCG, ii, 39a): Mk 12:44, Lk 8:4315:12, 3021:4, I Jo 3:17.†
SYN.: ζωή, is life intensive, "vita quâ vivimus," the vital principle; βίος, life extensive, "vita quam vivimus," (1) the period of life, (2) the means by which it is sustained. Hence, in cl., ζ., being confined to the physical life common to men and animals, is the inferior word (cf. zoology, biography). In NT, ζωή is elevated into the ethical and spiritual sphere (cf. Tr., Syn., § xxvii).

βουλευτής.g: a member of a city council, of the Sanhedrin
βουλευτής.long: a member of a city council, in NT of the Sanhedrin at Jerusalem.
βουλευτής.sd: an adviser, i.e. (specially) a councillor or member of the Jewish Sanhedrin
βουλευτής.as:
βουλευτής, -οῦ, ὁ
(< βουλεύω), [in LXX: Jb 3:1412:17 (יעץ)* ;]
a councillor, a senator; of a member of the Sanhedrin: Mk 15:34, Lk 23:50.†

βλάπτω.sd: properly, to hinder, i.e. (by implication) to injure
βλάπτω.as:
βλάπτω,
[in LXX: Pr 25:20, To 12:2, Wi 10:818:2, II Mac 12:22, IV Mac 9:7* ;]
to hurt, injure: c. acc., Mk 16:[18], Lk 4:35.†

βεβαιόω.long: I confirm, ratify, secure, establish; pass: I guarantee.
βεβαιόω.as:
βεβαιόω, -ῶ
(< βέβαιος), [in LXX: Ps 40 (41):12 (נצב hi.), 118 (119):28 (קוּם pi.), III Mac 5:42*;]
to confirm, establish, secure, of things (cl.): λόγον, Mk 16:[20]; ἐπαγγελίας, Ro 15:8; of persons (DCG, ii, 605): I Co 1:8, II Co 1:21. Pass., I Co 1:6, Col 2:7, He 2:313:9 (as an Attic legal term, to guarantee the validity of a purchase, establish or confirm a title; v. next word, Cremer, 139; cf. δια-β.).†

βρέφος.sd: an infant (properly, unborn) literally or figuratively
βρέφος.as:
** βρέφος, -ους, τό,
[in LXX: Si 19:11, I Mac 1:61, II Mac 6:10, III Mac 5:49, IV Mac 4:25*;]
1.an unborn child: Lk 1:41, 44.
2.a newborn child, a babe: Lk 2:12, 1618:15, Ac 7:19, I Pe 2:2; ἀπὸ βρέφους, from infancy, II Ti 3:15.†

βραχίων.der: properly, comparative of G1024 (βραχύς), but apparently in the sense of (to wield);
βραχίων.as:
βραχίων, -ὀνος, ὁ,
[in LXX, β. Κυρίου, freq. for זְרוֹעַ יהוָֹה ;]
the arm; as in OT, β. Κυρίου, metaph., for the Divine power: Lk 1:51, Jo 12:38(LXX), Ac 13:17.†

βουνός.as:
βουνός, -οῦ, ὁ (a Cyrenaїc word, Hdt., iv, 199),
[in LXX chiefly for גִּבְעָה;]
a hill: Lk 3:5(LXX)23:30.†

Βόος.long: Boaz, son of Salmon and Rahab, husband of Ruth, father of Obed.
Βόος.as:
Βοός and Βοές (RV, Βοάζ, Rec. Βοόζ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בֹּעַז),
Boaz (Ru 2:1): Mt 1:5, Lk 3:32.†

βυθίζω.long: I cause to sink; mid: I sink, submerge, drown.
βυθίζω.sd: to sink; by implication, to drown
βυθίζω.as:
** βυθίζω
(< βυθός), [in LXX: II Mac 12:4 * ;]
trans., to cause to sink, to sink: metaph., εἰς ὄλεθρον, I Ti 6:9; pass., to sink, intrans.: Lk 5:7.†

βλητέος.long: a verbal adj: one must put, that ought to be put.
βλητέος.as:
*† βλητέος, -α, -ον (gerundive of βάλλω),
(that which) one must put: Lk 5:38.†

βαθύνω.as:
βαθύνω
(< βαθύς), [in LXX for עמד: Ps 91 (92):5, Je 29 (49):830(49):30*;]
to deepen: Lk 6:48.†

βασίλειον.as:
βασίλειον, -ου, τό
(< βασίλειος, q.v.), [in LXX for הֵיכָל (Na 2:6, Da 6:18*), מַמְלָכָה (III Ki 3:114:8, IV Ki 15:19*), etc.;]
1. a capital city.
2. Freq. in pl., τὰ β., a palace: Lk 7:25.†

βουλή.sd: volition, i.e. (objectively) advice, or (by implication) purpose
βουλή.as:
βουλή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< βούλομαι), [in LXX freq. for עֵצָה ;]
counsel, purpose (in cl., esp. of the gods): Lk 23:51, Ac 4:285:3819:127:12, 42; pl., I Co 4:5; of the Divine purpose, He 6:17; τ. βουλὴν τ. θελήματος αὐτοῦ, Eph 1:11; β. τ. Θεοῦ, Lk 7:30, Ac 2:2313:3620:27.†

βαλλάντιον.der: probably remotely from G906 (βάλλω) (as a depository);
βαλλάντιον.as:
βαλλάντιον (Rec. βαλά-), -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX: Jb 14:17 (צְרוֹר), Pr 1:14 (כִּיס), To 1:148:2, Si 18:33א2*;]
a purse: Lk 10:412:3322:35, 36.†

βοῦς.sd: an ox (as grazing), i.e. an animal of that species ("beef")
βοῦς.der: probably from the base of G1006 (βόσκω);
βοῦς.as:
βοῦς, βοός, ὁ, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for בָּקָר;]
an ox, a cow: Lk 13:1514:5, 19Jo 2:14, 15I Co 9:9(LXX), I Ti 5:18.†

βορρᾶς.long: the north wind, hence: the North.
βορρᾶς.as:
βορρᾶς, -ᾶ (Attic contr. of Βορέας, the North wind personified),
[in LXX for צָפֹון;]
1.Boreas, the North wind.
2.the north: Lk 13:29, Re 21:13.†

βουλεύομαι.sd: to advise, i.e. (reflexively) deliberate, or (by implication) resolve
βουλεύομαι.kj: consult, take counsel, determine, be minded, purpose
βουλεύομαι.as:
βουλεύω
(< βουλή), [in LXX chiefly for יעץ;]
to take counsel, deliberate, resolve. In mid.,
1.to take counsel with oneself, consider: seq. εἰ, Lk 14:31.
2.to determine with oneself, resolve: c. inf., Ac 5:3327:39; c. acc., II Co 1:17; seq. ἵνα, Jo 11:5312:10 (cf. παρα-, συμ-).†

βύσσος.as:
βύσσος, -οῦ, ἡ (cf. Heb. בּוּץ),
[in LXX chiefly for שֵׁשׁ, בּוּץ ;]
byssus, a fine species of flax, also the linen made from it: Lk 16:19.†

βάπτω.sd: to whelm, i.e. cover wholly with a fluid; in the New Testament only in a qualified or special sense, i.e. (literally) to moisten (a part of one's person), or (by implication) to stain (as with dye)
βάπτω.as:
βάπτω,
[in LXX chiefly for טבל;]
(a)to dip: Lk 16:24, Jo 13:26 (ἐμβ-, L);
(b)to dip in dye, to dye: Re 19:13 (Rec.; ῥεραντισμένον, WH; περιρεραμμένον, T; ῥεραμμένον, Swete, in l., q.v.).†

βελόνη.as:
* βελόνη, -ῆς, ἡ
(< βέλος),
1.a sharp point, as of a spear.
2.a needle: Lk 18:25 (Rec. ῥαφίς, q.v.).†

βιωτικός.kj: of (pertaining to, things that pertain to) this life
βιωτικός.as:
* βιωτικός, -ή, -όν
(< βιός),
pertaining to life, hence, worldly (Field, Notes, 171): Lk 21:34, I Co 6:3, 4.†

βολή.long: a casting, throw; in acc: as measure of distance.
βολή.sd: a throw (as a measure of distance)
βολή.as:
βολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< βάλλω), [in LXX: Ge 21:16 (טחה), II Mac 5:3, III Mac 5:26 * ;]
a throw; λίθου β. (Thuc., v, 65, 2), a stone's throw: Lk 22:41.†

βραχύς.sd: short (of time, place, quantity, or number)
βραχύς.as:
βραχύς, -εῖα, -ύ,
[in LXX chiefly for מְעַט ;]
short;
(a) of time; short, little: βραχύ, Ac 5:34; μετὰ β., Lk 22:58; β. τι, a short time, He 2:7, 9 RV, mg.;
(b) of distance: Ac 27:28;
(c) of quantity or value, little, few: Jo 6:7, He 2:7, 9 RV, txt.; pl., διὰ βραχέων, in few words, He 13:22.†

βαθύς.long: deep (lit. and met.); in the depths of the early morning, while still very early; profound.
βαθύς.sd: profound (as going down), literally or figuratively
βαθύς.as:
βαθύς (gen. -έως, vernac., Lk 24:1; Bl., § 8, 5), -εῖα, -ύ,
[in LXX chiefly for עמק;]
deep; Jo 4:11; metaph., ὄρθρου βαθέως (v. supr.), early dawn, Lk 24:1; ὕπνος, Ac 20:9; τὰ β. τοῦ Σατανᾶ, Re 2:24.†

βραδύς.as:
* βραδύς, -εῖα, -ύ,
slow: εἰς τὸ λαλῆσαι, Ja 1:19; metaph., of the understanding: β. τ. καρδίᾳ, assoc. with ἀνόητος, Lk 24:25.†

βρώσιμος.as:
βρώσιμος, -ον
(< βρῶσις), [in LXX: Le 19:23, Ne 9:25, Ez 47:12 (מַאֲכָל)* ;]
eatable: Lk 24:41.†

βασιλικός.g: connected with a king, royal, regal
βασιλικός.long: connected with a king, royal, regal, (a) an officer in the service of the king, (b) the king's country.
βασιλικός.sd: regal (in relation), i.e. (literally) belonging to (or befitting) the sovereign (as land, dress, or a courtier), or (figuratively) preeminent
βασιλικός.as:
βασιλικός, -ή, -όν
(< βασιλεύς), [in LXX for מֶלֶךְ and its cognates;]
royal, belonging to a king: χώρα, Ac 12:20; ἐσθής, Ac 12:21; νόμος β., a supreme law, "a law which governs other laws and so has a specially regal character" (Hort), or because made by a king (LAE, p. 3673), Ja 2:8; τις, one in the service of a king, a courtier, Jo 4:46, 49 (WH, mg., βασιλίσκος).†

Βηθεσδά.long: Bethesda, name of a pool in Jerusalem.
Βηθεσδά.sd: house of kindness; Beth-esda, a pool in Jerusalem
Βηθεσδά.der: of Chaldee origin (compare H01004 and H02617);
Βηθεσδά.as:
Βηθεσδά, ἡ, indecl.
(deriv. uncertain, v. Westc. on Jo 5:2, and DB, i, 279),
Bethesda, a pool in Jerusalem: Jo 5:2, Rec. (Βηθζαθά, WH, Βηθσαϊδά, WH, mg.).†

βιβρώσκω.der: a reduplicated and prolonged form of an obsolete primary verb (perhaps causative of G1006 (βόσκω));
βιβρώσκω.as:
βιβρώσκω, poët, and late prose,
[in LXX for אכל;]
to eat: Jo 6:13.†

βάϊον.sd: a palm twig (as going out far)
βάϊον.der: a diminutive of a derivative probably of the base of G939 (βάσις);
βάϊον.as:
**† βαΐον, ου, τό
(also βὰϊον, another form of βὰϊς, from the Egyptian), [in LXX: I Mac 13:51*;], (freq. in Egyptian π., v. MM, Exp., x);
a palm-branch: Jo 12:13 (DB, i, 314).†

Βαρσαββᾶς.long: Barsabbas, son of Sabbas, a surname of Joseph and Judas.
Βαρσαββᾶς.sd: son of Sabas (or Tsaba); Bar-sabas, the name of two Israelites
Βαρσαββᾶς.der: of Chaldee origin (H01247 and probably H06634);
Βαρσαββᾶς.as:
Βαρσαββᾶς (Rec. -αβᾶς), -ᾶ
(Aram., son of Sabba),
Barsabbas:
1. the surname of one Joseph: Ac 1:23.
2. The surname of one Judas: Ac 15:22.†

βίαιος.as:
βίαιος, -α, -ον
(< βία), [in LXX for אָנַשׁ, עַז, צַר, etc.;]
violent: Ac 2:2.†

βάσις.sd: a pace ("base"), i.e. (by implication) the foot
βάσις.as:
βάσις, -εως, ἡ
(< βαίνω), [in LXX chiefly for אֶדֶן;]
1.a step (Æsch., al.).
2. Hence, a foot (Plat.; Wi 13:18): Ac 3:7.†

Βαρναβᾶς.long: Barnabas, a Cypriote Jew, uncle of John Mark; his other name was Joseph.
Βαρναβᾶς.sd: son of Nabas (i.e. prophecy); Barnabas, an Israelite
Βαρναβᾶς.as:
Βαρ-ναβᾶς, -α, ὁ
(Aram. בַּר, son, as prefix to another word interpreted in Ac 4:36, τῆς παρακλήσεως, perh. נְבוּאָה, wh., however, should be rendered by προφητεία as in II Es 6:14, LXX. Deiss., BS, 309 f., thinks Β. may be a variant of the name Βαρνεβοῦς, son of Nebo, found in a Syrian Inscr., altered with a view to disguising its origin; v. also Milligan, NTD, iii; Dalman, Gr., 142),
Barnabas: Ac 4:369:2711:22, 3012:2513-15, I Co 9:6, Ga 2:1, 9, 13, Col 4:10.†

βία.der: probably akin to G979 (βίος) (through the idea of vital activity);
βία.as:
βία, -ας, ἡ,
[in LXX for פֶּרֶךְ, etc.;]
strength, force, violence: Ac 5:2621:3524:727:41.†

βλάσφημος.sd: scurrilious, i.e. calumnious (against men), or (specially) impious (against God)
βλάσφημος.der: from a derivative of G984 (βλάπτω) and G5345 (φήμη);
βλάσφημος.as:
βλάσφημος, -ον
(< βλασ-, of uncertain deriv., v. Thayer, Boisacq; + φήμη, speech), [in LXX: Is 66:3 (מְבָרֵךְ אָוֶן), Wi 1:6, Si 3:16, II Mac 9:2810:4, 36 * ;]
(a)evil-speaking, slanderous, blasphemous: Ac 6:11, II Ti 3:2, II Pe 2:11 (cf. Ju 9);
(b) as subst. a blasphemer: I Ti 1:13 (Cremer, 570).†

βρύχω.long: I grind or gnash, as with the teeth for rage or pain.
βρύχω.sd: to grate the teeth (in pain or rage)
βρύχω.as:
βρύχω (Attic, βρύκω),
[in LXX: Jb 16:10(9), Ps 34 (35):1636 (37):12111 (112):10, La 2:16 (חרק)* ;]
1.to bite or eat greedily.
2.to gnash, grind, with the teeth: Ac 7:54.†

βυρσεύς.as:
*† βυρσεύς, -έως, ὁ (< βύρσα, a hide), late form for βυρσοδέψης,
a tanner: Ac 9:4310:6, 32.†

Βλάστος.long: Blastus, chamberlain of King Herod Agrippa I.
Βλάστος.sd: Blastus, an officer of Herod Agrippa
Βλάστος.der: perhaps the same as the base of G985 (βλαστάνω);
Βλάστος.as:
Βλάστος, -ου, ὁ,
Blastus, chamberlain of Agrippa: Ac 12:20.†

Βαριησοῦς.long: Bar-Jesus, the name of the magician and false prophet at Paphos in Cyprus; he is also called Elymas.
Βαριησοῦς.sd: son of Jesus (or Joshua); Bar-jesus, an Israelite
Βαριησοῦς.as:
Βαρ-ιησοῦς, -οῦ, ὁ
(Aram. בַּר־יֵשׁוּעַ, son of Joshua),
Bar-Jesus: Ac 13:6 (v.s. Ἐλύμας).†

Βενιαμίν.long: Benjamin, youngest son of Jacob, founder of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
Βενιαμίν.as:
Βενιαμίν, (Rec. -μίν), ὁ, indecl.
(Heb. בֶּנְיָמִין),
Benjamin: Ac 13:21, Ro 11:1, Phl 3:5, Re 7:8.†

Βιθυνία.long: Bithynia, a Roman province, north-west of Asia Minor and south-west of the Black Sea.
Βιθυνία.as:
Βιθυνία, -ας,
Bithynia, a province in Asia Minor: Ac 16:7, I Pe 1:1.†

Βέροια.long: Berea, a town of the province Macedonia.
Βέροια.der: perhaps a provincial from a derivative of G4008 (πέραν) (Perœa, i.e. the region beyond the coast-line);
Βέροια.as:
Βέροια, -ας, ἡ,
Berœa, a city of Macedonia: Ac 17:10, 13.†

βωμός.long: an altar, platform; a slightly-elevated spot.
βωμός.sd: properly, a stand, i.e. (specially) an altar
βωμός.as:
βωμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< βαίνω), [in LXX (Hex.) for מִזְבֵּחַ, in Proph., chiefly for בָּמָה ;]
1. any raised place, a platform.
2.an altar: Ac 17:23 (cf. θυσιαστήριον and v. DB, i, 75).†

Βεροιαῖος.sd: a Berœoean or native of Berœa

Βερνίκη.long: Bernice, daughter of Agrippa I and Kypros, and sister of M. Julius Agrippa II.
Βερνίκη.sd: victorious; Bernice, a member of the Herodian family
Βερνίκη.der: from a provincial form of G5342 (φέρω) and G3529 (νίκη);
Βερνίκη.as:
Βερνίκη
(elsewhere Βερενίκη, Macedonian form of Φερενίκη, cf. Veronica, Victoria), -ης, ἡ,
Bernice, Berenice, dau. of Herod Agrippa I: Ac 25:13, 2326:30.†

βίωσις.sd: living (properly, the act, by implication, the mode)
βίωσις.as:
**† βίωσις, -εως, ἡ
(< βιόω), [in LXX: Si prol.12 * ;]
manner of life: Ac 26:4.†

βραδυπλοέω.der: from G1021 (βραδύς) and a prolonged form of G4126 (πλέω);
βραδυπλοέω.as:
*† βραδυπλοέω, -ῶ
(< βραδύς, πλοῦς),
to sail slowly: Ac 27:7.†

βοήθεια.long: (a) abstr: assistance, (b) concr: (a technical term of nautical language), a help.
βοήθεια.sd: aid; specially, a rope or chain for frapping a vessel
βοήθεια.as:
βοήθεια, -ας, ἡ (v.s. βοηθέω),
[in LXX for עֵזֶר, etc. ;]
help: He 4:16; pl., helps, "frapping," a technical nautical term (MM, Exp., x; DB, ext., 367): Ac 27:17.†

βολίζω.g: I cast the line for sounding, I sound
βολίζω.long: I cast the line (for sounding), I sound.
βολίζω.as:
* βολίζω
(< βολίς, in sense of sounding-lead),
to heave the lead, take soundings: Ac 27:28.†

βούλημα.as:
βούλημα, -τος, τό
(< βούλομαι), [in LXX: Pr 9:10 (דַּעַת), II Mac 15:5, IV Mac 8:18*;]
purpose, will: Ac 27:43, Ro 9:19, I Pe 4:3.†
SYN.: θέλημα.

βάρβαρος.g: a foreigner who speaks neither Greek nor Latin
βάρβαρος.long: a foreigner, one who speaks neither Greek nor Latin; as adj: foreign.
βάρβαρος.as:
βάρβαρος, -ον
(prob. onomatop., descriptive of unintelligible sounds), [in LXX: Ps 113 (114):1 (לעז), Ez 21:31 (36) (בּער), II Mac 2:214:2510:4, III Mac 3:24*;]
barbarous, barbarian, strange to Greek language and culture (and also, after the Persian war, with the added sense of brutal, rude): Ac 28:2, 4, Ro 1:14, I Co 14:11, Col 3:11 (v. Lft., in l., and Notes, 249).†

βδελύσσομαι.sd: to be disgusted, i.e. (by implication) detest (especially of idolatry)
βδελύσσομαι.as:
βδελύσσω
(< βδέω, to stink), [in LXX chiefly for תּעב, שׁקץ;] >in cl., mid. only (Attic, -ττομαι);
to make foul; pass., Re 21:8; mid., to turn away in disgust from, to detest: Ro 2:22 (Cremer, 137).†

βέβαιος.der: from the base of G939 (βάσις) (through the idea of basality);
βέβαιος.as:
** βέβαιος, -ον (also -α, -ον;
< βαίνω), [in LXX: Es 3:13, Wi 7:23, III Mac 5:317:7, IV Mac 17:4*;]
firm, secure: ἄγκυρα, He 6:19; metaph., sure (esp. "in the sense of legally guaranteed security," Deiss., BS, 109; cf . two foll. words): ἐπαγγελία, Ro 4:16; ἐλπίς, II Co 1:6; λόγος, He 2:2; παρρησία, He 3:6; ἀρχή (τ. ὑποστάσεως), He 3:14; διαθήκη, He 9:17; κλῆσις κ. ἐκλογή, II Pe 1:10; comp. (-ότερος), προφητικὸς λόγος, II Pe 1:19.†

Βάαλ.long: Baal, chief deity of the Phoenicians and other Semitic nations.
Βάαλ.sd: Baal, a Phœnician deity (used as a symbol of idolatry)
Βάαλ.as:
Βάαλ (Rec. βαάλ), ὁ, ἡ, indecl. (Heb. בַּעַל, lord),
Baal: Ro 11:4(LXX). The fem. art. here agrees with the usage of LXX, where, following a similar Hebrew practice (בֹּשֶׁת for בַּעַל), αἰσχύνη appears to have been substituted in reading for the written Βάαλ (cf. III Ki 18:19), and to account for the freq. use of the fem. art. bef. Β. The usage, however, is not general, and in the passage cited in Ro (III Ki 19:18), LXX reads τῷ Β.†

βρόχος.long: a noose or snare; a cord.
βρόχος.as:
βρόχος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX: Pr 6:5 (יָד) 7:21 (חֵלֶק) 22:25 (מֹוקֵשׁ), III Mac 4:8 * ;]
a noose, a slip-knot, a halter: metaph., a restraint (not, as AV, R, txt., a snare): I Co 7:35.†

βραβεῖον.sd: an award (of arbitration), i.e. (specially) a prize in the public games
βραβεῖον.as:
* βραβεῖον, -ου, τό
(< βραβεύς, an umpire),
a prize in the games: I Co 9:24; metaph., of the Christian's reward, Phl 3:14.†

Βελιάρ.long: Belial, a demon, and in fact a name for Satan.
Βελιάρ.sd: worthlessness; Belial, as an epithet of Satan
Βελιάρ.as:
Βελιάρ, ὁ, indecl.
(another form of previous word, "due to harsh Syriac pronunciation," or else < Heb. בֵּל יַעַר, lord of the forest),
Beliar, a name of Satan: II Co 6:15 (v. DB, i, 269).†

βυθός.as:
βυθός, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX: Ex 15:5, Ne 9:11 (מְצוֹלָה), Ps 67 (68):2268 (69):2, 15106 (107):24 (מְצוּלָה)* ;]
1.the bottom.
2.the depth of the sea, the deep sea: II Co 11:25.†

βασκαίνω.g: I give the evil eye to, fascinate, bewitch, overpower
βασκαίνω.long: I give the evil eye to, fascinate, bewitch, overpower.
βασκαίνω.sd: to malign, i.e. (by extension) to fascinate (by false representations)
βασκαίνω.as:
βασκαίνω,
[in LXX: De 28:54, 56 (רעע), Si 14:6, 8*;]
1.to slander (Dem.).
2.to blight by the evil eye, to fascinate, bewitch: Ga 3:1.†

βέλος.sd: a missile, i.e. spear or arrow
βέλος.as:
βέλος, -εος, τό
(< βάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for חֵץ;]
a missile, a dart: Eph 6:16.†

βεβαίωσις.as:
βεβαίωσις, -εως, ἡ
(< βεβαιόω, q.v.), [in LXX: Le 25:23 (צְמִיתֻת), Wi 6:19*;]
confirmation: τ. εὐαγγελίου, Phl 1:7; εἰς β., He 6:16, a phrase freq. in π. of guarantee in a business transaction (Deiss., BS, 104 ff.; Cremer, 140).†

βραβεύω.long: (lit: to act as arbiter in the games), I rule, arbitrate.
βραβεύω.sd: to arbitrate, i.e. (genitive case) to govern (figuratively, prevail)
βραβεύω.as:
** βραβεύω
(< βραβεύς, an umpire), [in LXX: Wi 10:12 * ;]
(a) prop., to act as umpire; hence,
(b) generally, to arbitrate, decide (Isocr., Dem.; Lft., Col., l.c.; MM, s.v.): Col 3:15;
(c) in some late writers, to direct, rule, control (so in Col., l.c., acc. to Thayer, s.v., Meyer, in l.), (cf. κατα-βραβεύω).†

βέβηλος.sd: accessible (as by crossing the door-way), i.e. (by implication, of Jewish notions) heathenish, wicked
βέβηλος.der: from the base of G939 (βάσις) and (a threshold);
βέβηλος.as:
βέβηλος, -ον
(< βαίνω, whence βηλός, a threshold), [in LXX chiefly for חֹל;]
1.permitted to be trodden, accessible (v. DCG, ii, 422b); hence,
2. (opp. to ἱερός) unhallowed, profane: of things, I Ti 4:76:20, II Ti 2:16; of men, I Ti 1:9, He 12:16 (cf. κοινός; Cremer, 140).†

βαθμός.g: a step, a stage, a position
βαθμός.long: a step (of a stairway); hence: a stage in a career, a position.
βαθμός.as:
† βαθμός, -οῦ, ὁ, Ion. form of βασμός
(< βαίνω, to step), [in LXX I Ki 5:5 (מִפְתָּן), IV Ki 20:9, 10, 11 (מַעֲלָה), Si 6:36*;]
a step (IV Ki 20:9, 10, 11, of degrees of a dial); metaph., a degree, standing: I Ti 3:13.†

βραδύνω.long: I am slow, I delay, tarry.
βραδύνω.as:
βραδύνω
(< βραδύς), [in LXX: Ge 43:10 (מההּ hith.), De 7:10, Is 46:13 (אחר pi.), Si 32 (35):18 * ;]
1. trans., to retard (Soph., Is, l.c.).
2. More freq. intrans., to be slow, to tarry: I Ti 3:15, II Pe 3:9.†

βλαβερός.as:
βλαβερός, -ά, -όν
(< βλάπτω), [in LXX: Pr 10:26* ;]
hurtful: I Ti 6:9.†

βέλτιον.der: neuter of a compound of a derivative of G906 (βάλλω) (used for the comparative of G18 (ἀγαθός));
βέλτιον.as:
βελτίων, -ον (gen. -ονος), comp. of ἀγαθός,
[in LXX chiefly for טוֹב;]
neut. as adv., better, very well: II Ti 1:18 (also Ac 10:28 D). On elative use in these passages, v. M, Pr., 78, 236.†

βδελυκτός.as:
† βδελυκτός, ή, -όν
(< βδελύσσω), [in LXX: Pr 17:15 (תּוֹעֵבָה), Si 41:5, II Mac 1:27*;]
abominable, detestable: Tit 1:16 (Cremer, 137).†

βραχύ.sd: short (of time, place, quantity, or number)
βραχύ.as:
βραχύς, -εῖα, -ύ,
[in LXX chiefly for מְעַט ;]
short;
(a) of time; short, little: βραχύ, Ac 5:34; μετὰ β., Lk 22:58; β. τι, a short time, He 2:7, 9 RV, mg.;
(b) of distance: Ac 27:28;
(c) of quantity or value, little, few: Jo 6:7, He 2:7, 9 RV, txt.; pl., διὰ βραχέων, in few words, He 13:22.†

βοτάνη.as:
βοτάνη, -ῆς, ἡ
(< βόσκω), [in LXX for עֵשֶׂב,דֶשֶׁא,חָצִיר;]
1.grass, fodder.
2.green herb: He 6:7.†
SYN.: λάχανον, a garden herb, a vegetable.

Βαράκ.long: Barak, one of the judges of Israel.
Βαράκ.as:
Βαράκ, ὁ, indecl.
(Heb. בָּרָק),
Barak (Jg 4:6): He 11:32.†

βοηθός.as:
βοηθός, -ον (v.s. βοηθέω),
[in LXX chiefly for עזר ;]
1. (poët. -όος), hasting to the war-cry (Hom.).
2.helping, auxiliary; as subst. (Hdt.), a helper: He 13:6(LXX).†

βρύω.g: I cause to gush forth, send forth
βρύω.long: I cause to gush forth, send forth.
βρύω.sd: to swell out, i.e. (by implication) to gush
βρύω.as:
* βρύω, poët., late prose and vernac.,
to be full to bursting;
1. of the earth producing vegetation.
2. Of plants putting forth buds.
3. Of springs, to gush with water: Ja 3:11.†

βοή.sd: a halloo, i.e. call (for aid, etc.)
βοή.as:
βοή, -ῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX for זְעָקָה, etc. ;]
a cry: Ja 5:4.†

βασίλειος.g: courtiers, palaces, a body of kings, royal
βασίλειος.long: courtiers, palaces, a body of kings, royal.
βασίλειος.as:
βασίλειος, -ον (also -α, -ον;
< βασιλεύς), [in LXX; Ex 19:6, De 3:10 (מַמְלָכָה), Ex 23:22, Wi 18:15, III Mac 3:28, IV Mac 3:8*;]
royal: I Pe 2:9(LXX) (v. Hort, in l.).†

βιόω.as:
βιόω, -ῶ
(< βίος), [in LXX: Pr 7:29:6 (חיה), Jb 29:18, Wi 4:4א1, 12:23, Si 40:28, IV Mac 5:2217:18 * ;]
to spend life, to live: τ. χρόνον βιῶσαι (cl., more freq. 2 aor., -ναι), I Pe 4:2 (cf. Jb, l.c.).†
SYN.: ζάω (q.v.).

βλέμμα.long: a look, glance; sight and hearing.
βλέμμα.as:
* βλέμμα, -τος, τό
(< βλέπω),
a look, a glance: βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ, II Pe 2:8, sight and hearing, a sense not found for β. in Gk. lit., but perh. recognized in the vernacular (ICC, in l.)†

Βαλαάμ.long: Balaam, son of Beor of Pethor on the Euphrates, a soothsayer in the Old Testament.
Βαλαάμ.sd: Balaam, a Mesopotamian (symbolic of a false teacher)
Βαλαάμ.as:
Βαλαάμ, ὁ, indecl.
(Heb. בִּלְעָם), as in LXX (FlJ has ὁ βάλαμος);
Balaam (Nu 22-24): II Pe 2:15, Ju 11, Re 2:14.†

βόρβορος.as:
βόρβορος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX: Je 45(38):6 (טִיט)* ;]
mud, filth: II Pe 2:22.†

Βαλάκ.long: Balak, son of Zippor, King of Moab.
Βαλάκ.as:
Βαλάκ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בָּלָק),
Balak; (Nu 22:2): Re 2:14.†

βασανισμός.as:
** βασανισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< βασανίζω), [in LXX: IV Mac 9:611:2*;]
torture, torment: Re 9:514:1118:7, 10, 15.†

βιβλαρίδιον.as:
*† βιβλαρίδιον, -ου, τό
(dim. of βιβλάριον, dim. of βίβλος),
a little book: Re 10:2, 8 (WH, βιβλιόν, T2, 7βιβλιδάριον) 9, 10. Not hitherto found elsewhere.†

βότρυς.as:
βότρυς, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX for אֶשְׁכֹּל;]
a cluster of grapes: Re 14:18 (cf. στραφυλή) .†

βάτραχος.as:
βάτραχος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX: Ex 8, Ps 77 (78):45104 (105):30 (צְכַרִדֵּעַmisspelling of צְפַרְדֵּעַ n="H6854"), Wi 19:10*;]
a frog: Re 16:13.†

βύσσινος.sd: made of linen (neuter a linen cloth)
βύσσινος.as:
βύσσινος, -η, -ον
(< βύσσος), [in LXX chiefly for שֵׁשׁ, בּוּץ, etc. ;]
made of βύσσος, fine linen: Re 18:12, 1619:8, 14.†

βήρυλλος.long: a beryl, a precious stone of various colors, the best known being sea-green.
βήρυλλος.as:
**† βήρυλλος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ,
[in LXX: To 13:17 (-ύλλιον in Ex 28:20, שֹׁהַם)*;]
beryl, a jewel of sea-green colour: Re 21:20.†
